query: I am a private sector salaried employee working in Delhi. How is my House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption limit calculated under the 1962 rules?
persona_context: Private sector salaried employee residing in Delhi (metro city)
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 2A of the Income Tax Rules 1962, the HRA exemption for a salaried employee in Delhi (a metro city) is the least of: (a) actual HRA received, (b) rent paid in excess of 10% of salary, or (c) 50% of salary (since Delhi is a metro city; non-metros are 40%).
evaluation_criteria: States rent paid minus 10% of salary
Specifies least of the three is exempt

query: As a central government employee, how is the perquisite value of government-provided residential accommodation determined?
persona_context: Central government officer in government-allotted quarters
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 3(1) Table (Sl. No. 1), for Union or State Government employees, the perquisite value of unfurnished accommodation is the licence fee determined by the government in accordance with the rules framed by the government, reduced by the rent actually paid by the employee.
evaluation_criteria: Refers to licence fee determined by the Government
Mentions deduction of rent actually paid by employee

query: I am a private company employee living in a town with a population of 12 lakhs. My employer owns the apartment provided to me. What percentage of my salary is taken as the accommodation perk under the 1962 rules?
persona_context: Private sector employee provided employer-owned housing in a mid-sized city (population 12 lakhs)
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 3(1) of the 1962 rules, where the accommodation is owned by the employer in a city having a population exceeding 10 lakhs but not exceeding 25 lakhs (as per the 2001/2011 census depending on amendment), the perquisite value is 10% of salary (or 7.5% under the revised 2023 amendment for population between 15-40 lakhs), reduced by any rent recovered from the employee.
evaluation_criteria: Identifies population tier (between 10 to 25 lakhs / 15 to 40 lakhs)
States percentage of salary (10% or revised 7.5%)

query: I am a software engineer opting for the New Tax Regime under section 115BAC. Can I claim children education allowance and hostel allowance exemptions under Rule 2BB?
persona_context: Software engineer opting for New Tax Regime u/s 115BAC with school-going children
ground_truth_answer: No. Under Rule 2BB(3) of the Income Tax Rules 1962, an employee who has exercised an option under section 115BAC (New Tax Regime) is entitled to exemption ONLY in respect of allowances mentioned in sub-rule (1)(a) to (d) (tour/travel, daily allowance, conveyance, helper) and sub-rule (2) Table Sl. No. 11 (transport allowance for disabled employees). Children education allowance (Sl. No. 7) and hostel subsidy (Sl. No. 8) are NOT exempt under the New Tax Regime.
evaluation_criteria: Explicitly states Children Education and Hostel Allowance are NOT exempt under New Tax Regime
Identifies permitted allowances (conveyance, daily, tour, travel, handicap transport)

query: I am an employee claiming Leave Travel Concession (LTC) for a vacation in Singapore. Is my international flight exempt under Rule 2B?
persona_context: Salaried employee traveling abroad on holiday
ground_truth_answer: No. Under Rule 2B of the Income Tax Rules 1962, Leave Travel Concession (LTC) exemption under section 10(5) is strictly limited to travel to any place within India. Foreign/international travel expenses are not exempt.
evaluation_criteria: States LTC is strictly restricted to travel within India
Denies exemption for overseas / Singapore travel

query: I am a senior citizen aged 77 who receives only pension and interest income. Can I submit a declaration to my bank under Rule 26D so that no tax return is required to be filed?
persona_context: 77-year old pensioner wanting relief u/s 194P and Rule 26D
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 26D and Section 194P of the Income Tax Act, a specified senior citizen (who is a resident aged 75 years or more) having only pension income and interest income from the same specified bank can furnish a declaration in Form No. 12BBA to the specified bank. Since you are 77, you qualify to submit Form 12BBA under Rule 26D.
evaluation_criteria: Mentions age threshold (75 years or more)
States pension and interest income condition

query: I changed jobs during the previous year. What form must I submit to my current employer to declare salary and TDS from my previous employer under Rule 26A?
persona_context: Salaried employee switching employers mid-year
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 26A(1) of the Income Tax Rules 1962, an employee who has been employed under more than one employer during the financial year must furnish the details of salary due or received and tax deducted at source to the subsequent employer in Form No. 12B.
evaluation_criteria: Specifies furnishing details of previous employer salary and TDS

query: I work for a private company that provided me with a 1.8-litre engine car for both official and personal use, and the company pays all running and maintenance expenses. What is the monthly perquisite value added to my salary under Rule 3?
persona_context: Corporate manager with company-owned car (> 1.6L cubic capacity) used partly for personal purposes with employer-borne running expenses
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 3(2) Table (Sl. No. 1(1)(c)(ii)), where a motor car exceeding 1.6 litres cubic capacity is owned or hired by the employer, running and maintenance expenses are met by the employer, and it is used partly for official and partly for personal purposes, the perquisite value is Rs. 2,400 per month (plus Rs. 900 per month if a chauffeur/driver is provided).
evaluation_criteria: States monthly perquisite value of Rs. 2,400
Notes additional Rs. 900 per month if chauffeur is provided

query: Under the 2026 rules (Rule 280), if an employee opts for the new tax regime under section 202(4), which specific allowances remain exempt?
persona_context: Salaried employee operating under the 2026 direct tax regime exercising section 202(4) option
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 280(3) of the Income Tax Rules 2026, an employee who has exercised an option under section 202(4) is entitled to exemption ONLY in respect of allowances mentioned in sub-rule (1)(a) to (d) (travel/transfer allowance, tour daily allowance, conveyance allowance, helper allowance) and in sub-rule (2) [Table: Sl. No. 10] (transport allowance for visually impaired or orthopedically disabled employees).
evaluation_criteria: Specifies sub-rule (1)(a)-(d) allowances (travel, daily, conveyance, helper)
Specifies sub-rule (2) Sl. No. 10 (disability transport allowance)

query: I am a blind salaried individual. What is the monthly transport allowance exemption available to me under Rule 2BB of the 1962 rules?
persona_context: Visually impaired employee commuting to work
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 2BB(2) Table (Sl. No. 11), an employee who is blind or deaf and dumb or orthopedically handicapped with disability of lower extremities is entitled to a transport allowance exemption of Rs. 3,200 per month for commuting between residence and place of duty.
evaluation_criteria: States monthly exemption limit of Rs. 3,200
Identifies purpose: commuting between residence and work

query: How is the value of interest-free or concessional loan provided by employer for education/medical purposes calculated for a salaried employee under Rule 15 (2026 rules)?
persona_context: Salaried employee with company loan under 2026 rules
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 15 of the 2026 rules, the value of an interest-free or concessional loan is determined on the basis of the maximum monthly balance at the rate charged by State Bank of India. However, loans for medical treatment of specified diseases or petty loans not exceeding Rs. 20,000 are completely exempt from perquisite valuation.
evaluation_criteria: Refers to SBI benchmark lending rate
Mentions Rs. 20,000 threshold or medical treatment exemption

query: I realized I missed reporting my salary bonus for Financial Year (FY) 2019-20. Can I file an Updated Return of Income (ITR-U) under Rule 12AC of the 1962 rules?
persona_context: Salaried employee wanting to correct omitted income from FY 2019-20
fy_ay_context: User asks for FY 2019-20 (which corresponds to Assessment Year 2020-21)
temporal_constraint: Rule 12AC w.e.f. 29-04-2022 applies to AY commencing 1st April 2020 and subsequent years
ground_truth_answer: Yes. Financial Year (FY) 2019-20 corresponds to Assessment Year (AY) 2020-21. Under Rule 12AC(1) of the Income Tax Rules 1962 (inserted w.e.f. 29-04-2022), the return of income under section 139(8A) in Form ITR-U is eligible for the assessment year commencing on 1st April 2020 (AY 2020-21) and subsequent assessment years. Therefore, FY 2019-20 is eligible.
evaluation_criteria: Confirms AY 2020-21 is the first eligible assessment year under Rule 12AC

query: Can I file an updated return under Rule 12AC for income earned during Financial Year 2017-18?
persona_context: Salaried person querying an older financial year for ITR-U
fy_ay_context: User asks for FY 2017-18 (which corresponds to AY 2018-19)
temporal_constraint: Rule 12AC eligibility begins only from AY 2020-21 onwards
ground_truth_answer: No. Financial Year (FY) 2017-18 corresponds to Assessment Year (AY) 2018-19. Under Rule 12AC(1), Form ITR-U is applicable only for the assessment year commencing on the 1st day of April, 2020 (AY 2020-21) and subsequent assessment years. AY 2018-19 falls outside the temporal scope of Rule 12AC.
evaluation_criteria: Explicitly denies eligibility for FY 2017-18 / AY 2018-19

query: How did the Leave Travel Concession (LTC) exemption rules change between Rule 2B of the 1962 rules and Rule 278 of the 2026 rules regarding block years?
persona_context: Salaried employee comparing LTC rules across 1962 and 2026 regimes
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 2B of the 1962 rules, LTC exemption is available for 2 journeys in a block of four calendar years (commencing from calendar year 1986). Under Rule 278 of the 2026 rules, the statutory framework maintains the 2-journey exemption for Schedule III, structured in blocks as designated under the revised 2026 code provisions.
evaluation_criteria: Explains 2 journeys in a block of 4 calendar years
Highlights statutory transition from Section 10(5) to Schedule III

query: When did Rule 12AC come into force and by which amendment rules was it inserted into the 1962 Income Tax Rules?
temporal_constraint: Inserted by IT (Eleventh Amdt.) Rules, 2022, w.e.f. 29-4-2022
ground_truth_answer: Rule 12AC was inserted into the Income Tax Rules 1962 by the Income-tax (Eleventh Amendment) Rules, 2022, with effective date (w.e.f.) from 29th April, 2022.

query: Compare the valuation of company accommodation perks between 1962 Rule 3 and 2026 Rule 15 for a private sector employee in a major metro with population > 40 lakhs.
persona_context: Corporate employee analyzing rent-free accommodation valuation across 1962 and 2026 regimes
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 3 of the 1962 rules (post-2023 amendment), the perquisite value of employer-owned accommodation in cities having population > 40 lakhs as per the 2011 census is 10% of salary. Under Rule 15 of the 2026 rules, the valuation follows the modernized schedule under Section 15 with aligned population tiers and salary definitions.
evaluation_criteria: Identifies 10% salary cap for population > 40 lakhs in 1962 (revised)

query: What are the procedural steps to calculate tax relief under Rule 21A for salary received in arrears under section 89?
persona_context: Government / PSU employee receiving 3 years of salary arrears in a single lump sum
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 21A(1) and (2) of the Income Tax Rules 1962: (1) Calculate tax on total income including arrears in the year of receipt, (2) Calculate tax on total income excluding arrears in the year of receipt, to find the tax difference [A], (3) For each year to which arrears relate, calculate tax including and excluding additional salary to find tax difference [B], (4) Relief equals [A] minus [B] (if positive). The employee must furnish particulars in Form No. 10E under Rule 21AA.
evaluation_criteria: Explains Step 1 & 2 (tax with and without arrears in receipt year)
Explains Step 3 & 4 (tax in respective previous years)
